decisions.reason: After four years and two years without website visibility, the citrus harvesting crate no longer looks like an unresolved growth option, and its niche focus makes redeploying resources more attractive than keeping it alive.

The foldable large container line remains close to the firm's core reusable transport-packaging business, so despite weaker visibility its multiple-model platform still has enough strategic and learning value to keep open at modest incremental cost.
A low-prominence stackable crate line that disappeared from view for two years offers limited remaining option value, so management would likely rationalize it unless demand had clearly strengthened.

The medium-duty rackable pallet fits core capabilities but its weak visibility over time suggests the market has largely revealed its limited upside, making discontinuation slightly more likely than continuation.
The spill-retention pallet appears to have been an adjacent niche test, and once such an option shows little visible traction a large firm would usually exit and refocus on stronger core lines.
This pallet variant leverages existing know-how but looks too narrow and commercially unproven after several years, so the firm would more likely drop it than keep tying up attention and capacity.
